results.identification: A bullet‑point summary of the UK Conservative Party’s 2010 general election manifesto—‘Invitation to Join the Government of Britain’—derived from that manifesto (produced by the Conservative Party), though the wording here is an unofficial paraphrase/summary rather than the original text.
results.evidence: Repeated references to 2010-era UK Conservative policies: “Big Society,” Office for Budget Responsibility, emergency Budget/deficit reduction, elected police commissioners, GP‑led NHS commissioning, Cancer Drugs Fund, National Citizen Service, scrap ID cards/National Identity Register, ‘referendum lock’ and never join the Euro, restore earnings link for the state pension, bank levy/BoE supervision, Green Investment Bank/Green Deal, High Speed Rail while opposing Heathrow 3rd runway. These are all signature planks of the Conservatives’ 2010 general election manifesto.

results.identification: A third‑party summary of the UK Labour Party’s 2010 general election manifesto titled “A Future Fair for All,” derived from the official Labour Party manifesto.
results.evidence: The header explicitly says “Labour Party Manifesto 2010 — ‘A Future Fair for All’ (summary)”. The bullets match signature 2010 UK Labour pledges: 50p top rate and NI rise; Future Jobs Fund; Heathrow third runway with conditions; fixed‑line broadband levy; AV referendum; National Care Service; 0.7% aid by 2013; High Speed Rail; Green Investment Bank.

results.identification: An unofficial, bullet‑point synopsis of the UK Liberal Democrats’ 2010 General Election manifesto. The content is drawn from the party’s official 2010 manifesto, but the wording here is a later summary, not the original document.
results.evidence: Title line explicitly says “Liberal Democrat Manifesto 2010 – Summary”; hallmark 2010 Lib Dem policies listed, e.g. raising the income tax personal allowance to £10,000; introducing a mansion tax on property over £2m; scrapping ID cards and control orders; opposing new nuclear power; phasing out university tuition fees over six years; reviewing Trident rather than like‑for‑like replacement; adopting STV for the Commons and votes at 16; the ‘Freedom Bill’ civil liberties package; the Pupil Premium; and creating a UK Infrastructure Bank.

results.identification: An unofficial, third‑party bullet‑point summary of the UK Independence Party (UKIP) manifesto for the 2010 UK general election, derived from UKIP’s 2010 manifesto rather than the party’s official text.
results.evidence: The header explicitly says “UKIP Manifesto 2010 – Summary (under 500 words).” The content lists hallmark UKIP 2010 positions: leaving the EU; five‑year freeze on immigration; repeal of the Human Rights Act and leaving the ECHR; climate‑sceptic stance and repeal of the Climate Change Act; large defence increase and maintaining Trident; citizen’s pension; direct democracy and elected local boards; and transport ideas like a Thames Estuary hub airport.

results.identification: A secondary-source summary of the British National Party’s 2010 UK general election manifesto (‘Democracy, Freedom, Culture and Identity’), likely adapted from the British National Party article’s policy/2010 manifesto section on Wikipedia.
results.evidence: It explicitly opens with “The British National Party’s 2010 manifesto…” and lists hallmark BNP 2010 positions: halting all new immigration and promoting voluntary repatriation; leaving the EU; portraying Islam as incompatible with Western democracy and proposing bans on the burka, ritual slaughter, and new mosques; restoring corporal and capital punishment; reinstating a 200‑mile fishing limit; and nationalising telecoms infrastructure for universal 100 Mbps broadband. These are distinctive planks of the BNP’s 2010 general election manifesto, ‘Democracy, Freedom, Culture and Identity.’

results.identification: A neutral, bullet‑point summary of the UK Conservative Party’s 2010 General Election manifesto, ‘Invitation to Join the Government of Britain’ (published April 2010).
results.evidence: Multiple signature 2010 UK Conservative pledges appear: create the Office for Budget Responsibility and hold an emergency Budget within 50 days; scrap ID cards and limit DNA retention; recognise marriage in the tax system; set an annual cap on non‑EU migration; no new runways at Heathrow, Stansted or Gatwick; a bank levy; establish a Green Investment Bank and the Green Deal (~£6,500 per home); renew the nuclear deterrent; an EU ‘referendum lock’; 0.7% aid by 2013; Cancer Drugs Fund; GP‑led commissioning; pupil premium; abolish regional housing targets; replace RDAs with Local Enterprise Partnerships; Border Police Force; reduce MPs by ~10%; Fair Fuel Stabiliser; R&D tax credits focused on hi‑tech SMEs; corporation tax to 25%/20% for small firms; four CCS plants; supermarket ombudsman; targeted badger control.

results.identification: A condensed summary of the UK Labour Party’s 2010 General Election manifesto, "A Future Fair for All," published by the Labour Party (April 2010).
results.evidence: References tightly match distinctive Labour 2010 pledges: "Future Jobs Fund (200,000 jobs)"; "Referenda on Alternative Vote and a reformed, elected second chamber; fixed‑term parliaments"; "a third runway at Heathrow with conditions"; "Create UK Finance for Growth (£4bn)"; "Transform the Post Office into a People’s Bank"; "National Care Service... from 2011 free home care for highest needs"; "re‑link Basic State Pension to earnings from 2012"; "0.7% of national income to aid by 2013 in law"; "two‑thirds shareholder support" for takeovers; "Green Investment Bank"; "1% public‑sector pay cap (2011–13)."

results.identification: An anonymised, policy‑only summary of the UK Liberal Democrats’ 2010 General Election manifesto (“Change that works for you. Building a fairer Britain”), originating from the Lib Dem 2010 manifesto.
results.evidence: Flagship Liberal Democrat 2010 pledges appear throughout: raise the income tax personal allowance to £10,000; a 1% levy on property value above £2m (“mansion tax”); restore the state pension earnings link via a ‘triple lock’; scrap ID cards; no like‑for‑like Trident replacement; oppose new nuclear; £2.5bn Pupil Premium; phase out tuition fees over six years; convert Northern Rock to a building society; per‑plane duty and cancel Heathrow’s third runway; STV for MPs and votes at 16; end child detention in the asylum system; elected police authorities; PostBank; ‘eco‑cashback’ and a £3.1bn green stimulus.

results.identification: A policy summary of the United Kingdom Independence Party (UKIP) 2010 UK General Election manifesto, ‘Empowering the People,’ published by UKIP (ukip.org) in April 2010.
results.evidence: Distinctive UKIP 2010 policies appear throughout: leaving the EU and ECHR; a 31% flat tax merging income tax and employee NI; abolishing VAT and replacing it with a Local Sales Tax shared with councils; a non–means-tested Citizen’s Pension of at least £130/week at 65; repeal of the Climate Change Act and expansion of nuclear to up to 50% of electricity; leaving the Common Fisheries Policy with a 200‑mile EEZ and landing all catches; English‑only sittings at Westminster; protecting imperial weights and measures; St George’s Day as a holiday; a Thames Estuary hub airport; school and health vouchers; abolishing Ofsted; and strong border controls including restoring the Primary Purpose Rule.

results.identification: A bullet‑point summary of the British National Party’s (BNP) 2010 UK general election manifesto, from the RationalWiki article on the British National Party (section: “Summary of the 2010 manifesto”).
results.evidence: Header explicitly says “Summary of the 2010 manifesto (policies only, with ideological framing removed)”. The policy mix matches the British National Party’s 2010 UK general election manifesto: immediate EU withdrawal; halting most immigration and specifically from Muslim‑majority countries; repeal of race/equalities laws; withdrawal from the ECHR and repeal of the Human Rights Act; reintroduction of corporal and capital punishment; ban on non‑stunned ritual slaughter; 90 mph motorway limit; restoration of a 200‑mile fishing zone; maglev rail; nationalising telecoms infrastructure for universal 100 Mbps; compulsory one‑year community service for school leavers; “voluntary resettlement” incentives; protection of pubs with supervised smoking rooms. The exact phrasing “with ideological framing removed” and the bullet‑pointed, sectioned summary are characteristic of the RationalWiki page on the BNP, which includes a section titled precisely this.
